Both poly reds close, and the fix is the law rather than a workaround for it.

graph's occurs write-guard reported from inside graph_bind's arm. A diagnostic
performed inside an arm resolves OUTER of its own install — so it sailed past
any capture bracket installed deeper, which is exactly where
infer_fn_speculative installs poly_capture. held_has_poly was therefore false,
the Mycroft retry never fired, and round 1's honest refusal was what the user
saw. The file half-knew it already: "an arm's performs resolve OUTER" is
written three times around that guard, drawn as a conclusion about what the
arm may RENDER and never about what it may REPORT.

THE SHAPE IS THE HOLES PAIR, ONE CONCERN OVER. graph_handler gains
guard_diags state; the guard pushes its triple instead of performing;
graph_guard_drain hands the list to whoever asks; infer_fn drains and narrates
one statement after the judgment that provoked it. An arm may note; only the
body may narrate. The empty case — the overwhelming one — resumes without a
state rebind, so a judgment where no bind refused pays nothing.

home rather than a drain at each of the five call sites.

mentl/88dc655:
Pure addition. Nothing references it yet (lexer + parser
rewrite is step 2 of Ω.4). Lands SYNTAX.md's Token spec into
the type system as the canonical declaration the next two
files implement against.

Token wrapper mirrors the AST Node wrapper:
  type Node  = N(NodeBody, Span, Int)
  type Token = Tok(TokenKind, Span)

Same wrapper discipline at every layer. Uniform accessors:
  fn token_kind(t) = let Tok(k, _) = t; k
  fn token_span(t) = let Tok(_, s) = t; s

TokenKind enumerates 69 variants per SYNTAX.md:
  • 24 keywords (TFn / TLet / … / TTrue / TFalse)
  • 5 identifiers + literals (TIdent / TInt / TFloat /
    TString / TDocComment) with payload
  • 15 two-character operators (TEqEq / TArrow / TFatArrow /
    TPlusPlus / all five pipe verbs / TAndAnd / TOrOr /
    TColonColon)
  • 23 single-character operators and punctuation (TLParen /
    TRParen / TLBrace / TRBrace / … / TQuestion)
  • 2 layout (TNewline / TEof)

H6 discipline propagates to the lexical layer: a parser match
on Token must enumerate every variant; adding a new variant
fails compilation across every dispatch site until handled.

Next (Ω.4 step 2): lexer + parser coupled rewrite implementing
this exact enumeration.

mentl/888e7fa:
Two changes in wasm_emit.lux that came out of root-causing the Arc 2
self-miscompilation:

(1) emit_expr's LLet handler now mirrors emit_stmt's: if the name is
    in ctx_globals, emit global.set, not local.set. Previously emit_expr
    unconditionally emitted local.set, which masked the actual ctx_globals
    bug for state updates inside expression-position blocks (handler
    arm bodies, ResumeExpr's update_stmts). Wasn't the root cause but
    would have produced UNRESOLVED locals in nested-block paths even
    after the destructuring fix landed.

(2) Removed the `let mark = heap_save(); emit_fn(...); heap_restore(mark)`
    bracket around per-fn emission in emit_fn_list. In the Rust VM these
    are no-ops; in WASM they bracket genuine allocations. During the
    Arc 2 hunt this looked like the bug (it can wipe Snoc-tree slice
    intermediates if ctx is accessed during emit_fn). The actual bug
    was elsewhere — but the bracket also doesn't earn its keep: per-fn
    intermediate allocations are bounded, the bump allocator never
    reclaims anyway between fns, and removing it gave a cleaner story
    for "what could possibly be wiping ctx."

clob/88827f4:
src/eval/bench_suite.rs runs the full ablation matrix across axes:
{seeds} × {adaptive on/off} × {modules present/absent} × {router
pristine/trained} and emits a TSV row per cell (run_id, seed,
adaptive, n_modules, router, tokens, mean_nll, j_per_nat, tok/s,
joules).

Each cell loads a fresh model from disk (no leakage across
ablations), optionally installs critic/confidence-head/meta-critic
from side-files, optionally applies trained router weights, and
optionally loads crystal modules from a directory. Runs the eval
pass, measures J/nat via the existing TdpProxyMeter, and records
one BenchCell.

Core helpers:
  - cartesian_option_paths([]) = [None]; with k paths it's
    [None, Some(p0), Some(p1), ...], giving k+1 cells per axis.
  - summarize_by_axis aggregates cells by (adaptive, modules-present,
    router-state), averaging mean_nll and j_per_nat across seeds —
    the pivot view that makes ablation deltas readable at a glance.
  - emit_tsv writes a stable fixed-precision TSV (float format
    matches across runs so diffs are meaningful).

clob bench-suite subcommand wires it up:
  --model / --eval-corpus / --seeds 1,2,3
  --critic / --confidence-head / --meta-critic  (all optional)
  --routers-trained a.bin,b.bin     # plus the implicit pristine cell
  --modules-dirs d1,d2              # plus the implicit empty-modules cell
  --max-tokens / --adaptive-max-extra / --adaptive-z
  --out bench.tsv

Emits a manifest sidecar like all other write-subcommands.

Mean_nll is identical across cells because adaptive can't fire

stoop/88c0642:
Every run of this workflow has failed since it was added, on main and on
this branch alike, each in one to three seconds with no downloadable
logs. That shape is a job rejected before its first step, not a failing
check: the workflow file is valid ASCII, the repository is public so
minutes are not the constraint, check.sh needs only bash and finishes in
ninety milliseconds, and it passes against a pristine clone of the
pushed tree.

The one thing the job did that could be refused up front was reach for
actions/checkout. A repository whose Actions policy restricts marketplace
actions rejects that reference at startup and writes no logs, which is
the symptom exactly. So the workflow now fetches the commit with git
itself and uses no third-party actions at all.

That is worth doing even if the policy turns out innocent. check.sh
enforces a page that makes zero external requests; the job enforcing it
should not need a network dependency of its own to start. A first step
that only echoes proves the runner produced output at all, so if this
still fails the failure is account or repository configuration rather
than anything in the tree, and the logs will say so.
